claim: On factual QA, a linear probe on the hidden state between chain of thought and answer has ECE 5-38x lower than verbalized confidence across four benchmarks and two model families.
stance_target: L2: probe versus verbal readout in reasoning models (non-code)
scope_conditions: TriviaQA, EntityQuestions, NQ-open, SimpleQA-Verified; Qwen3-14B and Ministral-3-8B-Reasoning-2512; 1,000 questions and 10 traces each
quoted_support: a linear probe on the hidden state between the chain of thought and the answer is substantially better calibrated: its expected calibration error is 5–38 × lower than that of the verbalized score across four benchmarks and two model families.

claim: Used to pick among N sampled answers, the probe nearly ties majority voting and falls far short of the oracle: internal states answer how certain am I well and which answer is right poorly.
stance_target: L3: probe confidence not a good selector
quoted_support: Internal states answer “how certain am I” well and “which answer is right” poorly, so the signal should be reported as a confidence rather than used to select answers.
